rv.q: The lighting slides with her mood from austere and clinical to a lurid orange and music sometimes drowns out her attempts to communicate. Wilson feels her way through her character’s volatile psychological state with great dexterity.
For 75 minutes we see this sad soul in a high-rise flat, talking on the telephone to her ex-lover. All that is visible of the flat is an unfurnished corridor.

But Ivo van Hove’s weird, monochrome production of a weird, monochrome play, cuts her off from the audience behind a massive glass picture window, literally boxing her in so it’s very tough to make an emotional connection. It looked like an incredible acting masterclass might have been happening behind the glass but I just wasn’t feeling any of it.
